grh_0c72553d6adbcb7f4c64.title: Care and Feeding of a Sex Symbol
paragraphs: Hollywood talent agent Harry Silverman is under pressure to find a client who can revive his own flagging fortunes when he notices Susie, an actress whose looks have made her a sex symbol but have kept people from taking her acting seriously. Susie is used to agents treating her as an object and is suspicious of Harry's offer to represent her. He brings her home to meet his wife and children, trying to prove that his interest is professional, while discovering that Susie's appetite, family, pet cheetah and astrological adviser make managing her anything but simple. Harry nevertheless becomes convinced that there is a real performer behind the image and promises to build publicity around her without losing sight of her acting ambitions. After her astrologer warns that their signs are incompatible, Susie decides to take the chance anyway and signs Harry's management contract, giving both of them a possible new start.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on February 27, 1979. It is listed as episode 17 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Stacy O'Brien, Vance Colvig, Alan Young, Brian Miller, and Fletcher Markle. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, and Andy Griffith as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].
This version is based on [[work|work.sears.10f88ad0a7def0b3|Care and Feeding of a Sex Symbol]]. Shirley Gordon is credited as author.

grh_0c8c0773ce50e496ec83.title: Nothing but the Truth
paragraphs: Young stockbroker Bob Bennett wagers that he can tell nothing but the truth for twenty-four hours, putting $10,000 at stake just as he is surrounded by clients, friends and his boss's family. Absolute honesty quickly turns a weekend gathering into chaos as Bob blurts out opinions and secrets he would normally soften or conceal, including his feelings for the boss's daughter Gwen. A last-minute argument over the clock seems to cost him the bet, but a corrected time proves he has won both the money and Gwen.

grh_0c00af0e8576cdf57b8f.title: Clay Pigeon
paragraphs: Harry returns to New York and becomes entangled with gangster Cato, who possesses incriminating photographs that can be used to blackmail Governor Hadley into granting valuable concessions. Harry appears to join Cato and demands half the deal, but at the governor's office Cato turns violent and Harry stops him during an attempt on Hadley's life. Harry keeps the damaging negatives long enough to make the governor worry that the blackmail has merely changed hands. Later, alone in a dark alley, he burns the photographs rather than exploit them, proving more honest than anyone expected.

paragraphs: Three tobacconists are murdered in succession in the same East End waterfront shop, leading Holmes to suspect the premises rather than the victims.
